mainTopic: The slavery in מצרים, the righteous women who earned the redemption, and the Hebrew midwives
overview: The גמרא keeps explaining the פסוקים at the start of ספר שמות about the slavery in מצרים. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמואל בר נחמני argue whether בְּפָרֶךְ means 'with a soft mouth' or 'with crushing.' רבא and רבי יונתן add that the work grew harsher over time and that men's and women's jobs were swapped. רב עוירא then teaches that ישראל were redeemed in the merit of the righteous women. He tells how they cared for their husbands in the fields, gave birth under the apple tree, and how הקדוש ברוך הוא protected the babies until they recognized Him at the sea. Next the גמרא discusses the midwives שפרה and פועה: who they were (יוכבד with מרים or with אלישבע), פרעה's signs to them, and how they refused him and kept the babies alive. Their excuse that Jewish women are חיות is explained as 'like animals,' which give birth without help. Their reward of 'houses' is explained as כהונה and לויה or מלכות through דוד. The amud ends by working out who כלב's father was: חצרון, with 'בן יפנה' as a nickname and קנז as his stepfather.

steps.title: Two meanings of the word בְּפָרֶךְ
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads בְּפָרֶךְ as בְּפֶה רַךְ, 'with a soft mouth.' רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads it as בִּפְרִיכָה, 'with crushing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: On the word בְּפָרֶךְ: רבי אלעזר says it means 'with a soft mouth.' רבי שמואל בר נחמני says it means 'with crushing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two אמוראים who disagree about what the word בְּפָרֶךְ in the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר splits the word into two words, פֶּה רַךְ, a soft mouth. That means the Egyptians tricked בני ישראל into slavery with sweet talk. רבי שמואל בר נחמני connects it to the root פרך, crushing, so the slavery was harsh and backbreaking.

keyTerms.meaning: The word in the פסוק usually translated 'with rigor'
With a soft mouth, meaning with gentle persuasion
With crushing, meaning with harsh, breaking labor

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying the slavery was easy. He is explaining how it started: with soft words that slowly trapped them.

phrases.english: "With rigor"
phrases.notes: This finishes a quote from שמות 1:13 that started before this section.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: with a soft mouth.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: בִּפְרִיכָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says: with crushing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the running explanation of the פסוקים about the slavery in מצרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two readings of בְּפָרֶךְ: soft persuasion (רבי אלעזר) or crushing labor (רבי שמואל בר נחמני).

steps.title: The work started with bricks and grew to all field labor
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the order of the פסוק: first the Egyptians had them work with mortar and bricks, and later they added every kind of field work.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they made their lives bitter with hard work, with mortar and bricks, and so on.' רבא says: at first it was 'with mortar and bricks,' and in the end it was 'and with every kind of work in the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק, and רבא explains why it lists bricks first and then all field work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the order of the פסוק as an order in time. The slavery began with one type of work, building, and grew into every kind of labor. So the burden kept getting heavier over time.

keyTerms.meaning: At first... and in the end

phrases.english: "And they made their lives bitter with hard work,
with mortar and with bricks, etc."
Rava said: at first, "with mortar and with bricks,"
and in the end, "and with every work in the field."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the same passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The slavery got worse step by step: first building work, then every kind of field work.

steps.title: Swapping men's work and women's work
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני quotes רבי יונתן: the second בְּפָרֶךְ means the Egyptians gave men women's jobs and gave women men's jobs.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All their work that they made them do with rigor.' רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: they would swap men's work to women and women's work to men.
steps.whatsHappening: The end of the same פסוק says בְּפָרֶךְ again, and רבי יונתן explains what kind of harshness it means here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק uses בְּפָרֶךְ a second time, it must be adding something new. רבי יונתן says the cruelty was giving each person work they were not used to. Work that does not fit you is crushing even if it is not heavier.

phrases.aramaic: ״אֵת כׇּל עֲבֹדָתָם אֲשֶׁר עָבְדוּ בָהֶם בְּפָרֶךְ״,
phrases.english: "All their work which they made them do with rigor,"

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
that they would switch men's work to women
and women's work to men.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the end of the same פסוק that רבא was explaining.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second בְּפָרֶךְ means giving people work that did not suit them: men's jobs to women and women's jobs to men.

steps.title: Even רבי אלעזר agrees the second בְּפָרֶךְ means crushing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that even רבי אלעזר, who read the first בְּפָרֶךְ as 'soft mouth,' must agree that the second one means crushing labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to the one who said that there it means 'with a soft mouth,' here it certainly means 'with crushing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects back to the disagreement in step 1 and shows that it only applies to the first פסוק, not to this one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second פסוק is all about the actual hard labor: bricks, field work, and swapped jobs. So reading 'soft mouth' does not fit there. רבי אלעזר's 'soft mouth' reading is limited to the first פסוק, which talks about how the slavery began.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: The first בְּפָרֶךְ is debated (soft mouth or crushing). The second בְּפָרֶךְ is crushing according to everyone.

phrases.english: And even according to the one who says
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר from step 1.

phrases.english: there, "with a soft mouth,"
phrases.notes: "There" is the first פסוק, שמות 1:13; "here" is שמות 1:14.

phrases.english: here it is certainly "with crushing."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר נָמֵי הָתָם בְּפֶה רַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the step 1 disagreement together with רבי יונתן's explanation of the second בְּפָרֶךְ.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement about בְּפָרֶךְ is only about the first פסוק; in the second פסוק everyone agrees it means crushing labor.

steps.title: Redeemed in the merit of righteous women
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא teaches that בני ישראל were redeemed from מצרים because of the righteous women of that generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא taught: in reward for the righteous women who lived in that generation, בני ישראל were redeemed from מצרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching: רב עוירא states that the redemption from מצרים came in the merit of the righteous women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא described how hard the slavery was. Now it turns to how the redemption was earned. רב עוירא gives the main claim first and then explains it in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: In reward for, in the merit of

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source that the גאולה from מצרים came through the merit of the women of that generation.

phrases.english: Rav Avira taught:
In reward for the righteous women
who were in that generation,
Israel was redeemed from Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from describing the slavery to explaining why the redemption came.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption from מצרים came in the merit of the righteous women of that generation.

steps.title: The miracle of the fish in the water jugs
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא begins describing what the women did. When they went to draw water, הקדוש ברוך הוא put small fish in their jugs, so they came home and cooked two pots: one of hot water and one of fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they went to draw water, הקדוש ברוך הוא arranged small fish for them in their jugs. They drew up half water and half fish, and came and put two pots on the fire, one of hot water and one of fish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוירא starts explaining his claim from step 5 with a story about how the women were helped. The next step continues the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The women went out in their daily work, and הקדוש ברוך הוא sent them food along with the water. They used it to prepare two pots, one hot water and one fish. This sets up the rest of the story, which explains what they did with these and why it was so meritorious.

keyTerms.meaning: They place a pot on the fire

phrases.english: At the time when they would go to draw water,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, would arrange for them
small fish in their jugs,
and they would draw up half water and half fish,
and they would come and put two pots on the fire,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חַמִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל דָּגִים.
phrases.english: one of hot water and one of fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the story that explains רב עוירא's claim about the righteous women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא helped the women with fish in their water jugs, and they prepared two pots, hot water and fish.

steps.title: The women care for their husbands in the fields
steps.stepSummary: The women bring the food to their husbands in the field, wash them, anoint them, feed them, give them drink, and are intimate with them among the field borders. A פסוק in תהלים is quoted as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The women would bring the food to their husbands in the field. They would wash them, rub them with oil, feed them, give them drink, and be with them as husband and wife between the field borders, as the פסוק says: 'When you lie between the borders.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוירא continues his story. The women take the fish and hot water from Step 6 out to their husbands and take care of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The men were worn out by hard labor in the fields, so the women came to them there. They revived their husbands with bathing, oil, food and drink, and kept family life going. The פסוק's words 'between the borders' are read as describing exactly this scene in the fields.

keyTerms.meaning: They would anoint, rubbing someone with oil
Were intimate with (a polite way of saying it)
Between the borders or fences of the fields

phrases.english: And they would bring [it] to their husbands in the field,
phrases.notes: "It" means the hot water and fish they cooked back in Step 6.

phrases.english: and they would bathe them, and anoint them with oil,
and feed them, and give them to drink,
and be intimate with them between the borders,
phrases.notes: Here שפתים means the borders or fences that divide the fields.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "When you lie between the borders, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story directly from Step 6: what the women did with the food they cooked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The women revived their husbands in the fields and kept family life alive. This is based on 'אם תשכבון בין שפתים'.

steps.title: The reward: the plunder of מצרים
steps.stepSummary: Because of 'lying between the borders,' בני ישראל earned the plunder of מצרים. The second half of the same פסוק, about a dove covered in silver and gold, is the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a reward for 'lying between the borders,' Israel earned the riches of מצרים, as the פסוק continues: 'the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with shimmering gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the rest of the same פסוק as the reward for what the women did: silver and gold, meaning the wealth taken from מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק describes the act, and the second half describes the reward. The dove stands for בני ישראל, and the silver and gold are the riches they left מצרים with. This ties the women's devotion to the actual redemption, just as רב עוירא said in Step 5.

phrases.english: As a reward for "you lie between the borders,"
Israel merited the plunder of Egypt,
as it is stated: "The wings of a dove are covered with silver,
and her feathers with shimmering gold."

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׂכַר תִּשְׁכְּבוּן בֵּין שְׁפַתָּיִם זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבִיזַּת מִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the פסוק quoted in Step 7 and reads its second half as the reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the merit of the women's devotion, בני ישראל received the plunder of מצרים.

steps.title: Giving birth secretly under the apple tree
steps.stepSummary: Once pregnant, the women returned home. When it was time to give birth, they went out to the field and gave birth under the apple tree, as the פסוק in שיר השירים says.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they became pregnant, they would come home. When it was time to give birth, they would go out and give birth in the field under the apple tree, as the פסוק says: 'Under the apple tree I awakened you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to the births: the women went out to the fields to give birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving birth out in the field kept the babies hidden from the Egyptians, who wanted to kill the Jewish baby boys. The פסוק from שיר השירים, which mentions an apple tree and a mother in labor, is read as describing these births.

keyTerms.meaning: The time for them to give birth

phrases.english: And once they became pregnant, they would come to their homes,
and when the time came for them to give birth,
they would go and give birth in the field under the apple tree,
as it is stated: "Under the apple tree I awakened you, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the timeline: after the time in the fields comes pregnancy and birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The women gave birth in the fields under the apple tree, based on the פסוק in שיר השירים 8:5.

steps.title: Heaven sends help to clean the newborns
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא sends someone from heaven to clean and tidy the babies the way a midwife does. The source is the פסוק in יחזקאל about a baby whose navel was not cut and who was not washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא would send someone from heaven to clean the babies and make them look nice, like a midwife does for a newborn, as the פסוק says: 'On the day you were born, your navel was not cut, and you were not washed in water to be cleaned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The babies were born alone in a field with no human midwife, so הקדוש ברוך הוא sent heavenly help to care for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל describes a newborn that no person took care of. The גמרא reads it as showing there was no human midwife in מצרים, so help came straight from heaven instead.
steps.confusionAlert: Here חיה means a midwife, not an animal.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹלֵחַ מִשְּׁמֵי מָרוֹם
phrases.english: And the Holy One, Blessed be He, would send from the heavens above
someone who would clean them and tidy them,
like a midwife who tidies the newborn,
as it is stated: "And as for your birth, on the day you were born,
your navel was not cut,
nor were you washed in water to be cleaned, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹלֵחַ מִשְּׁמֵי מָרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains who cared for the babies born alone in the field in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heavenly help cleaned the newborns in place of a midwife, based on יחזקאל 16:4.

steps.title: Two stones of oil and honey to feed the babies
steps.stepSummary: The heavenly helper gathers two round stones for the babies, one giving oil and one giving honey. The source is 'He nursed him honey from a rock, and oil.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He would gather two round stones for them, one of oil and one of honey, as the פסוק says: 'He nursed him with honey from a rock, and oil.'
steps.whatsHappening: After cleaning the babies, the heavenly helper also feeds them miraculously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים says honey and oil were nursed from a rock. The גמרא reads this literally for the babies in מצרים: two stones flowed with oil and honey, and the babies nursed from them.

phrases.english: And he would gather for them two round stones,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן וְאֶחָד שֶׁל דְּבַשׁ,
phrases.english: one of oil and one of honey,
as it is stated: "And He nursed him with honey from a rock, and oil, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the heavenly care from Step 10: first cleaning, now feeding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The babies were miraculously fed oil and honey from stones, based on דברים 32:13.

steps.title: The ground swallows the babies to save them
steps.stepSummary: When the Egyptians found the babies and came to kill them, a miracle happened and the babies were swallowed into the ground. The Egyptians then plowed over them with oxen. The source is 'On my back the plowers plowed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Egyptians noticed them, they came to kill them. But a miracle happened: the babies were swallowed into the ground. The Egyptians brought oxen and plowed over them, as the פסוק says: 'On my back the plowers plowed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The danger arrives: the Egyptians find the hidden babies, and הקדוש ברוך הוא hides them inside the earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ground protected the babies, but the Egyptians still tried to destroy them by plowing over the spot. The פסוק in תהלים about plowers plowing 'on my back' is read as describing this.

keyTerms.meaning: On top of them (literally, on their backs)

phrases.english: And once the Egyptians noticed them,
they would come to kill them,
but a miracle happened for them and they were swallowed into the ground,
and they would bring oxen and plow on top of them,
as it is stated: "On my back the plowers plowed, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁמַּכִּירִין בָּהֶן מִצְרִים בָּאִין לְהוֹרְגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the danger that came after the babies were born and cared for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The babies were miraculously hidden in the ground from the Egyptians, based on תהלים 129:3.

steps.title: The babies sprout up like grass
steps.stepSummary: After the Egyptians left, the babies sprouted out of the ground like grass of the field. The source is 'I made you numerous like the growth of the field.'
steps.simpleTranslation: After the Egyptians left, the babies would sprout up and come out like the grass of the field, as the פסוק says: 'I made you as numerous as the plants of the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The miracle is completed: once the danger passes, the hidden babies come back up out of the earth alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plowing in Step 12 was supposed to destroy them, but just like plowed ground grows plants, the babies came up like grass. The פסוק in יחזקאל about growing like the plants of the field is read as describing this. The story keeps going in the next steps, which follow the children as they grow up and reach the sea.
steps.whatToRemember: רב עוירא's whole story shows that the righteous women's devotion, both caring for their husbands and having children despite the danger, is the merit that brought the redemption from מצרים. הקדוש ברוך הוא answered their faith with miracles at every stage: birth, care, feeding, and protection.

phrases.english: After they would leave,
the babies would sprout up and come out like the grass of the field,
as it is stated: "I made you numerous as the growth of the field."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַחַר שֶׁהוֹלְכִין הָיוּ מְבַצְבְּצִין וְיוֹצְאִין כְּעֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the miracle from Step 12: the babies hidden in the ground come back up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The babies came out of the ground alive and grew numerous like plants of the field, based on יחזקאל 16:7.

steps.title: The grown babies come home in big groups
steps.stepSummary: Once the babies grew up, they came home in large flocks. This is learned by reading a word in the פסוק in יחזקאל differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the babies grew up, they came back to their homes in huge groups, like flocks of sheep. The פסוק says 'you came with excellent beauty (בעדי עדיים).' Don't read it that way. Read it as 'in flocks and flocks (בעדרי עדרים).'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues from the babies sprouting out of the ground. Now they grow up and return home in big groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the next words of the same פסוק in יחזקאל used in the earlier steps. The גמרא uses an אל תקרי, a 'don't read it this way, read it that way.' It changes עדיים (beauty) into the similar-sounding עדרים (flocks), which shows the children came home in large numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Don't read it as…' This reads a word in a פסוק with different vowels or letters to learn something extra.

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the written פסוק is wrong. The written words stay the same. The גמרא is pointing to an extra layer of meaning hidden in the sound of the word.

phrases.english: And once they grow up
they come in flocks upon flocks to their homes,
as it says: 'And you increased and grew up'
'and you came with excellent beauty,'
do not read 'with excellent beauty,'
but rather 'in flocks upon flocks.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁמִּתְגַּדְּלִין בָּאִין עֲדָרִים עֲדָרִים לְבָתֵּיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after sprouting from the ground (step 13), the children grow up and return home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The grown children came home in large groups, learned from reading בעדי עדיים as בעדרי עדרים.

steps.title: These children recognized הקדוש ברוך הוא first at the sea
steps.stepSummary: At the splitting of the sea, these same children were the first to recognize הקדוש ברוך הוא, as the פסוק says 'This is my God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When הקדוש ברוך הוא showed Himself at the sea, these children recognized Him first, as it says: 'This is my God, and I will glorify Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last piece of the story about the babies. It ties their childhood miracles to קריעת ים סוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זה, 'this one,' sounds like pointing at someone you already know. The children had been cared for by הקדוש ברוך הוא when they were babies, so at the sea they could point and say 'This is my God.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is my God and I will glorify Him' (from אז ישיר)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole story shows הקדוש ברוך הוא personally caring for the babies in מצרים. That care is why they were the first to recognize Him at the sea.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁנִּגְלָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל הַיָּם,
phrases.english: And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, revealed Himself at the sea,
they recognized Him first,
phrases.notes: 'They' means those same babies from the story, now grown up.

phrases.english: as it says: 'This is my God, and I will glorify Him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁנִּגְלָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל הַיָּם הֵם הִכִּירוּהוּ תְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story of the babies by linking it to the splitting of the sea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The children saved in the fields recognized הקדוש ברוך הוא first at the sea.

steps.title: Who were the two Hebrew midwives? רב and שמואל disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about פרעה speaking to the Hebrew midwives. רב and שמואל argue about how the two midwives were related.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the king of מצרים said to the Hebrew midwives…' רב and שמואל disagree. One says they were a woman and her daughter. The other says they were a daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the next פסוק in שמות about the midwives. It presents a disagreement about who they were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the midwives שפרה and פועה, but the גמרא assumes these were not their usual names. The question is which real women they were. Here we only learn the family relationship each side holds. The actual names come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'one said… and the other said' (we don't know which אמורא said which)

phrases.english: 'And the king of Egypt said'
'to the Hebrew midwives, etc.'
phrases.notes: שמות 1:15. The 'etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק, which names them שפרה and פועה.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree:
one says: a woman and her daughter,
and one says: a daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in שמות and starts a new discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: the midwives were either a mother and daughter, or a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law.

steps.title: Naming the midwives on each side
steps.stepSummary: Mother and daughter means יוכבד and מרים. Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law means יוכבד and אלישבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'a woman and her daughter' means יוכבד and מרים. The one who says 'a daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law' means יוכבד and אלישבע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly which women each opinion has in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that one midwife was יוכבד. They argue only about the second one. One side says it was her daughter מרים. The other says it was her daughter-in-law אלישבע, the wife of אהרן.

keyTerms.meaning: mother of משה, אהרן and מרים
wife of אהרן, so יוכבד's daughter-in-law

phrases.english: The one who says a woman and her daughter —
means Yocheved and Miriam,
and the one who says a daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law —
means Yocheved and Elisheva.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ יוֹכֶבֶד וּמִרְיָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the names behind each relationship from step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific women does each opinion mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mother-daughter = יוכבד and מרים. Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law = יוכבד and אלישבע.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the mother-and-daughter view: שפרה is יוכבד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought that matches the view that the midwives were a mother and daughter. It begins by saying that שפרה is יוכבד, named for how she cared for newborns.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא matches the one who says 'a woman and her daughter.' It teaches: שפרה is יוכבד. Why was she called שפרה? Because she would clean up and tidy (משפרת) the newborn baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support one side of the רב and שמואל disagreement. It starts by explaining who שפרה was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the ברייתא only says that שפרה is יוכבד. Both opinions already agree on that. The support for the mother-and-daughter view will come from how the ברייתא names the second midwife. The name שפרה is read as coming from לשפר, to make nice, describing how she tidied the newborns.

keyTerms.meaning: 'a ברייתא is taught that matches the one who says…' This formula brings support for one side.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the support is already finished here. Both sides agree שפרה is יוכבד, so the proof depends on who the ברייתא says פועה was.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in line with the one who says a woman and her daughter,
for it is taught: Shifrah — this is Yocheved,
and why was she called Shifrah?
Because she would tidy up the newborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the mother-and-daughter opinion from steps 16 and 17.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the midwives were a woman and her daughter (יוכבד and מרים).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא identifying שפרה as יוכבד, which goes on to name the second midwife.

steps.title: A second reason for the name שפרה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא offers another explanation: she was called שפרה because the Jewish people were fruitful and multiplied in her days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'שפרה' — because the Jewish people were fruitful and multiplied (שפרו ורבו) in her days.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the same ברייתא, a second explanation is given for why יוכבד was called שפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason connected שפרה to tidying the babies. This one connects it to פרו ורבו, 'be fruitful and multiply.' Because of her work saving babies, the Jewish people grew in her time.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'Shifrah' —
because Israel was fruitful and multiplied in her days.
phrases.notes: The name שפרה is being read as שֶׁ־פָּרוּ, 'that they were fruitful.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר שִׁפְרָה שֶׁפָּרוּ וְרָבוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיָמֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason for the name שפרה inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שפרה can also be read as 'Israel was fruitful and multiplied in her days.'

steps.title: פועה is מרים, named for soothing the newborn
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the second midwife, פועה, is מרים. She got this name because she made soothing sounds while delivering babies.
steps.simpleTranslation: פועה is מרים. Why was she called פועה? Because she would coo softly and bring out the baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from שפרה (יוכבד) to the second midwife, פועה, and tells us she is מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as שפרה's name was explained by how she cared for babies, פועה's name is explained the same way. The word פועה is read as making soft, calming sounds during a birth. This fits the view of the midwives as mother and daughter (יוכבד and מרים).

keyTerms.meaning: The name of the second midwife in the פסוק

phrases.english: "Puah": this is Miriam.
And why was she called "Puah"?
Because she would make soothing sounds
and bring out the baby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from שפרה to פועה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פועה is מרים, named for soothing newborns during delivery.

steps.title: Second reason for the name פועה: מרים's prophecy
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives another reason for the name פועה. מרים spoke out with רוח הקודש that her mother would give birth to the savior of Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: she was called פועה because she spoke out with רוח הקודש and said, "My mother will one day give birth to a son who will save ישראל."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a second reading of the name פועה, this time based on מרים's prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here פועה is read as "speaking out" rather than "cooing." The son she predicted is משה. This matches the pattern of step 19, where שפרה also got a second explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Divine inspiration, a form of prophecy

phrases.english: Another explanation: "Puah":
because she would speak out through divine inspiration
and say: My mother is destined
to give birth to a son who will save Israel.

steps.whatToRemember: The two midwives' names each get two explanations. One explanation is about caring for babies, and the other is about something bigger: Israel growing (שפרה) or the coming savior (פועה).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different meaning for the same name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פועה means she spoke out prophecy about the birth of Israel's savior.

steps.title: What does the word אׇבְנָיִם mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes פרעה's order to the midwives and asks about the strange word אבנים in that פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he said: When you deliver the Hebrew women, etc." What does אׇבְנָיִם mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק and asks a word question. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבנים usually sounds like "stones," which does not obviously fit a birth scene. So the גמרא asks what פרעה meant when he told the midwives to look at the אבנים.

keyTerms.meaning: When you deliver babies (said to midwives)
The unclear word in the פסוק, related to "stones"

phrases.english: "And he said: When you deliver
the Hebrew women, etc."
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says to look at the "אבנים," which is the word the גמרא is about to ask about.

phrases.english: What does "ovnayim" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the names of the midwives and moves on to פרעה's instructions to them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word אבנים in פרעה's command.

steps.title: רבי חנן: the thighs turn cold as stones
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן explains that פרעה gave the midwives a sign: when a woman is about to give birth, her thighs become cold like stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנן said: He gave them a great sign. He told them: when a woman crouches to give birth, her thighs turn cold like stones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: אבנים means "stones," and it refers to a sign that birth is about to happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer keeps the simple meaning of אבנים as stones. פרעה was teaching the midwives how to tell that a birth is starting, so they would be ready to act.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the word

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanan said:
He gave them a great sign.
phrases.notes: "He" is פרעה, and "them" means the midwives.

phrases.english: He said to them: When she crouches to give birth,
her thighs become cold like stones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנָן: סִימָן גָּדוֹל מָסַר לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about אבנים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אבנים refers to the thighs turning stone-cold, which is a sign that birth is starting.

steps.title: Another view: אׇבְנָיִם like the potter's wheel
steps.stepSummary: Others explain אבנים from a פסוק in ירמיהו about a potter's wheels. A potter sits with his work between his thighs, and in the same way a woman giving birth has the baby between her thighs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it is like the פסוק "I went down to the potter's house, and he was working on the wheels." A potter has a thigh on each side and the block in the middle. So too a woman giving birth has a thigh on each side and the baby in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different meaning of אבנים by comparing it to the same word in another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here אבנים is not "stones" but the potter's wheel, which sits between his legs. The word describes the birthing position, with the baby coming out between the thighs. It is a different answer from רבי חנן's cold-stone sign.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces another opinion
The block or base the potter works on

phrases.english: And some say: as it is written:
"And I went down to the potter's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִנֵּה הוּא עוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה עַל הָאׇבְנָיִם״,
phrases.english: and behold, he was doing work on the wheels,"
Just as this potter:
a thigh here and a thigh there
and the block in the middle,
so too a woman:
a thigh here and a thigh there
and the baby in the middle.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two answers together. רבי חנן says אבנים means stones (cold thighs). The second view says it means a potter's wheel (the birthing position).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same question, different from רבי חנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אבנים is like the potter's wheel, which describes the birthing position with the baby between the thighs.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: how to tell a boy from a girl at birth
steps.stepSummary: On the words "if it is a son, kill him," רבי חנינא says פרעה gave a sign: a boy is born face down, and a girl face up.
steps.simpleTranslation: "If it is a son, kill him." רבי חנינא said: He gave them a great sign. A boy comes out face down, and a girl comes out face up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with the same פסוק and explains how the midwives were supposed to know right away if the baby was a boy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק assumes the midwives can tell a boy at the moment of birth. רבי חנינא fills in how: by which way the baby's face is turned. This let them act immediately, before the mother noticed.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the sign

phrases.english: "If it is a son, you shall kill him."
Rabbi Chanina said:
He gave them a great sign:
a boy: his face is downward;
a girl: her face is upward.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנן (step 23) and רבי חנינא (here) are two different people with similar names. Each gives a different "great sign."
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא, סִימָן גָּדוֹל מָסַר לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרעה taught the midwives that a boy is born face down and a girl face up, so they could identify boys right away.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say אֲלֵיהֶן instead of לָהֶן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about the midwives fearing God and asks why it uses the word אליהן instead of the simpler להן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The midwives feared God and did not do as he spoke אליהן.' It should have said להן, 'to them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices an odd word in the פסוק and asks why it was used. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal way to say 'he spoke to them' is דבר להן. The פסוק instead uses אליהן, which can mean 'about them' or 'upon them.' The גמרא assumes the unusual word must be there to teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: About them / upon them (the unusual word)

phrases.english: "And the midwives feared God

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עָשׂוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אֲלֵיהֶן וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and did not do as he spoke about them, etc."
It should have said "to them"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the midwife פסוקים, moving to the next פסוק after פרעה's command.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק uses אליהן rather than להן.

steps.title: פרעה tried to make the midwives sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that the word אליהן teaches that פרעה asked the midwives to sin with him, and they refused.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: This teaches that פרעה asked them to do a sinful act, and they did not give in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers the question about the strange word. He says it hints that פרעה tried to get the midwives to sin with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אליהן carries a sense of closeness, so he reads it as hinting at a forbidden relationship. The midwives' 'fear of God' now includes refusing פרעה personally, not only refusing to kill the babies.

keyTerms.meaning: That he asked / demanded of them
And they did not give in

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
This teaches that he asked them for a sinful act
phrases.notes: He means פרעה tried to get the midwives to sin with him.

phrases.english: and they did not give in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אליהן hints that פרעה demanded a sinful act from the midwives, and they refused.

steps.title: The midwives even fed the babies
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'they kept the children alive' as meaning the midwives also gave the babies water and food.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they kept the children alive.' A ברייתא taught: Not only did they not kill them, they even gave them water and food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the end of the same פסוק. It teaches that the midwives actively cared for the babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already said they 'did not do as he spoke,' meaning they did not kill. So 'they kept the children alive' must add something more: they took care of the babies, giving them water and food.

phrases.english: "And they kept the children alive."

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: לֹא דַּיָּין שֶׁלֹּא הֵמִיתוּ אוֹתָן,
phrases.english: A ברייתא taught: Not only did they not kill them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיוּ מַסְפִּיקוֹת לָהֶם מַיִם וּמָזוֹן.
phrases.english: but they would even provide them with water and food.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא לֹא דַּיָּין שֶׁלֹּא הֵמִיתוּ אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The midwives did not only spare the babies; they also gave them water and food.

steps.title: What does חָיוֹת mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the midwives' answer to פרעה and asks what the word חיות means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the midwives said to פרעה: The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women...' What does חיות mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the midwives' excuse to פרעה and asks about the word חיות. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The midwives said the Jewish women are חיות, so they give birth before the midwife arrives. The word is unclear and could mean 'midwives' or 'animals.' The גמרא asks which meaning fits.

keyTerms.meaning: For they are not like the women
The unclear word in the פסוק

phrases.english: "And the midwives said to Pharaoh
that [the Hebrew women] are not like the [Egyptian] women, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 1:19. The rest of the פסוק says כי חיות הנה, and that is the word the גמרא asks about.

phrases.english: What does "chayot" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next פסוק, the midwives' reply to פרעה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word חיות.

steps.title: It cannot mean actual midwives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests חיות means real midwives and rejects it, because even a midwife needs another midwife when she gives birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means actual midwives, does a midwife not need another midwife to deliver her baby?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one meaning of חיות, 'midwives,' and knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that the Jewish women are like midwives themselves, so they need no help. But that makes no sense, since a midwife giving birth still needs someone else to deliver her. So this reading cannot explain why they did not need help.

phrases.english: If you say it means actual midwives,
phrases.notes: In the language of חז״ל, חיה is a word for a midwife.

phrases.english: is that to say a midwife does not need
another midwife to deliver her baby?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא חַיּוֹת מַמָּשׁ אַטּוּ חַיָּה מִי לָא צְרִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects a first answer to the question of step 29.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even a midwife needs another midwife to give birth, so the reading does not explain why the women needed no help.

steps.title: The Jewish nation is compared to animals
steps.stepSummary: The midwives told פרעה that the Jewish nation is compared to animals, which give birth without help. The גמרא lists the animal images given to the שבטים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they told him: This nation is compared to an animal. יהודה is a lion's cub, דן a snake, נפתלי a deer, יששכר a donkey, יוסף an ox, and בנימין a wolf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true meaning: חיות means 'animals.' It backs this up with the animal comparisons in the ברכות to the שבטים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the excuse makes sense: animals give birth on their own, and the Jewish women did too. The list of פסוקים shows that the תורה itself compares the שבטים to animals, so the midwives' claim had a real basis.
steps.whatToRemember: The midwives fought פרעה in three ways: they refused his sinful demand, they fed the babies, and they gave a clever excuse. The Jewish women are like animals, which give birth without a midwife.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two meanings of חיה. In step 30 it meant 'midwife' and was rejected. Here it means 'animal.'

phrases.english: Rather, they said to him:
This nation is compared to an animal:
phrases.notes: The point is that animals give birth without a midwife's help.

phrases.english: Judah — "a lion's cub";
Dan — "Dan shall be a snake";
"Naftali is a deer let loose";
"Issachar is a strong-boned donkey";
Joseph — "a firstborn ox";
"Benjamin is a wolf that tears prey."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמְרוּ לוֹ אוּמָּה זוֹ כְּחַיָּה נִמְשְׁלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting 'midwives' in step 30, gives the correct meaning, 'animals.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חיות means animals: the Jewish nation is compared to animals, which give birth without help, as shown by the animal images of the שבטים.

steps.title: Every tribe is compared to an animal
steps.stepSummary: Some שבטים have their own animal image in the פסוקים. For those that don't, a general פסוק compares the whole Jewish nation to a lioness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever has an animal image written about him has it written. Whoever does not have one written about him is still covered by what is written: 'How your mother was a lioness; she crouched among lions.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the midwives' answer from the last step. It shows that every שבט, not only some, is compared to an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list in step 31 left out a few שבטים. The גמרא fills the gap with a פסוק that calls the whole nation a lioness. This way the midwives' claim covers all Jewish women.

keyTerms.meaning: the one about whom it is written

phrases.english: The one about whom it is written — it is written about him.
phrases.notes: He means the שבטים who already got their own animal image in the list.

phrases.english: And the one about whom it is not written — it is written about him:
"How your mother was a lioness
among lions she crouched, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of animal images begun in step 31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The whole Jewish nation is compared to animals, so the midwives' answer applies to every Jewish woman.

steps.title: What houses did ה׳ make for the midwives
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ה׳ made 'houses' for the midwives. רב and שמואל argue whether this means houses of כהונה and לויה or houses of מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And because the midwives feared God, He made them houses.' רב and שמואל disagree. One says: houses of priesthood and Levites. The other says: houses of royalty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the midwives' reward. It brings a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about what the 'houses' were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Houses' here means family lines that come from the midwives. One view says the family line of כהנים and לוים. The other says the royal family line. The next steps explain each view.

phrases.english: "And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God,
that He made them houses."
Rav and Shmuel disagree:
One said: houses of priesthood and Levites,
and one said: houses of royalty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the midwives' answer to פרעה to their reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two views of the midwives' reward: families of כהונה and לויה, or families of מלכות.

steps.title: Priesthood and Levites means אהרן and משה
steps.stepSummary: The view of houses of כהונה and לויה is talking about אהרן and משה, who came from יוכבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says houses of priesthood and Levites means אהרן and משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first view. The houses of כהונה and לויה are אהרן and משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views about the midwives (steps 16–17) agree that one of them was יוכבד. יוכבד was the mother of אהרן, the כהן גדול, and of משה, from שבט לוי. So the כהנים and לוים come from her.

keyTerms.meaning: אהרן and משה, sons of יוכבד

phrases.english: The one who says houses of priesthood and Levites —
means Aaron and Moses.
phrases.notes: Both were sons of יוכבד, one of the two midwives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first opinion from step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which family line counts as the 'houses of כהונה and לויה'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אהרן and משה, the sons of יוכבד.

steps.title: דוד comes from מרים
steps.stepSummary: The view of houses of מלכות means דוד, who comes from מרים. The proof is that כלב married אפרת, and דוד is called the son of an אפרתי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says houses of royalty means דוד, who also comes from מרים. It says: 'עזובה, כלב's wife, died, and כלב took אפרת, who bore him חור.' And it says: 'דוד was the son of that אפרתי man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second view and proves it from פסוקים. It shows that דוד, the king, comes from מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof links two פסוקים. כלב married אפרת, who is מרים, and had children with her. דוד is called the son of an 'אפרתי,' so he comes from אפרת, which means מרים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next steps, which deal with כלב's family because he is the link between מרים and דוד.

phrases.english: And the one who says houses of royalty —
David also comes from Miriam,
as it is written: "And Azubah, the wife of Caleb, died,
and Caleb took to himself Ephrath,
and she bore him Hur."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:19. The גמרא explains later that אפרת is מרים.

phrases.english: And it is written: "And David was the son of that Ephrathite man, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and proves the second opinion from step 33.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א 2:19 (כלב married אפרת) together with שמואל א 17:12 (דוד son of an אפרתי).

steps.title: A פסוק about כלב's family
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק calling כלב 'the son of חצרון' and listing his wives and children.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And כלב the son of חצרון had children from עזובה his wife and from יריעות, and these were her sons: ישר, שובב, and ארדון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about כלב's family. This sets up the next move: questions about who כלב's father really was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק names כלב's father as חצרון. Elsewhere, though, the תורה calls him the son of יפנה, and the next step raises that problem.

phrases.english: "And Caleb, the son of Hezron, had children
from Azubah, a wife, and from Jerioth;
and these were her sons: Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָלֵב בֶּן חֶצְרוֹן הוֹלִיד אֶת עֲזוּבָה אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side discussion about כלב, who was mentioned in the proof in step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק calls כלב the son of חצרון.

steps.title: Isn't כלב the son of יפנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the פסוק: how can it call כלב 'son of חצרון' when elsewhere he is called 'son of יפנה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Son of חצרון? He is the son of יפנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two פסוקים about the name of כלב's father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ספר במדבר, כלב is called 'בן יפנה.' A person can't have two different fathers, so one of the names needs explaining.

phrases.english: Son of Hezron?
He is the son of Jephunneh!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the name given in the פסוק quoted in step 36.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק calls him 'בן יפנה,' so the two names seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: יפנה is a nickname
steps.stepSummary: 'בן יפנה' is not his father's name. It is a nickname meaning he turned away from the plan of the מרגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is called 'בן יפנה' because he turned away from the advice of the spies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'יפנה' is a description, not a real father's name. His real father was חצרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יפנה sounds like 'פנה,' which means 'turned away.' כלב turned away from the bad report of the מרגלים, so the תורה gives him this name of praise.

keyTerms.meaning: the plan or advice of the spies

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'בן יפנה' here as a different father. The גמרא is saying it is a nickname, and his real father is חצרון.

phrases.english: He is a son who turned away from the counsel of the spies.
phrases.notes: A play on words: יפנה sounds like פנה, 'turned away.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a name as a descriptive nickname
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יפנה was כלב's actual father, which would contradict 'בן חצרון.'
steps.terutzMaskana: חצרון was his father; 'בן יפנה' praises him for turning away from the מרגלים.

steps.title: But כלב is called the son of קנז
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new problem: a פסוק calls עתניאל 'son of קנז, כלב's brother,' so it sounds like כלב was also a son of קנז.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, he is the son of קנז, as it says: 'And עתניאל son of קנז, כלב's brother, captured it.'
steps.whatsHappening: Even after the first answer, the גמרא finds another problem. A third name, קנז, seems to be כלב's father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If עתניאל is the son of קנז and is כלב's brother, then it seems כלב is also a son of קנז. That clashes with חצרון being his father.

keyTerms.meaning: and still, there is still a problem

phrases.english: But still: he is the son of Kenaz,
as it is written: "And Othniel, the son of Kenaz, captured it,
Caleb's brother"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a further challenge that the answer in step 38 does not solve.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חצרון was כלב's father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עתניאל son of קנז is called כלב's brother, which suggests כלב's father was קנז.

steps.title: כלב was קנז's stepson
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that כלב was the stepson of קנז. That is why he is linked to קנז even though his real father was חצרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He was the stepson of קנז.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the problem. קנז raised כלב as a stepson, so כלב and עתניאל were brothers through their mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלב's mother later married קנז, and עתניאל was born from that marriage. So עתניאל is 'כלב's brother' through the mother, and כלב is connected to קנז only as a stepson. חצרון stays his real father.
steps.whatToRemember: כלב's real father was חצרון. 'בן יפנה' is a nickname for turning away from the מרגלים, and he was the stepson of קנז.

phrases.english: Rava said:
He was the stepson of Kenaz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 39.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כלב was the son of קנז, which would contradict 'בן חצרון.'
steps.terutzMaskana: כלב was קנז's stepson; he shared a mother with עתניאל.
